page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 x86_64 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs with symmetric multithreading enabled. System memory totals 64.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Networking interfaces provide a baseline throughput of 20 Gbps. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage and contains no discrete GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating attached network volumes for persistent storage requirements.

Hardware capabilities include support for advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 formats, alongside dedicated cryptographic acceleration extensions including VAES and SHA-NI. In benchmark assessments, the AMD EPYC architecture exhibits upper-quartile performance in single-core and multi-core metrics, achieving top-tier scores in Geekbench single-core (2019.0), Geekbench multi-core (16728.0), and PassMark CPU encryption tests. General system performance remains balanced across middle-tier percentiles for multithreaded decompression, memory bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and Redis throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, ecs.c8ae.8xlarge provides high compute density tailored for parallel execution without allocating excess memory capacity. The primary tradeoff lies in the absence of ephemeral high-speed local NVMe storage, meaning all data persistence relies over the 20 Gbps network link. This configuration serves compute-heavy processing jobs, continuous integration and build systems, backend application hosting, and distributed batch processing workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized cloud instance powered by the AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at 3.4 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs, it pairs 64.0 GB of memory at a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on remote block storage. Architectural features include AVX-512 instructions (with VNNI and BF16 support) alongside cryptographic accelerators like VAES and SHA-NI. In benchmark evaluations, it demonstrates strong single-core and multi-core performance, excelling in PassMark encryption, text processing, and image processing routines, while maintaining solid throughput across web serving and Redis workloads. The compute-dense configuration offers balanced compute efficiency for CPU-intensive tasks without incurring memory-heavy overheads, making it suited for application servers, microservices, batch processing, and CI/CD pipelines.
